fiscal_rows.existing: The amount necessary for the initial implementation, charged against the available appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives; no amount stated.
fiscal_rows.consideration: About P107.1 million to P196.8 million in the first year for a Secretariat of 76 to 124 positions: PS P66.7 million to P132.9 million, MOOE P29.5 million to P46.8 million and CO P11.0 million to P17.0 million (one-time).
fiscal_rows.recommendation: The initial requirement may be charged to the available appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives, as provided, but the amount should be stated, consistent with SB No. 1624, so that it can be programmed within the two chambers' budgets.
fiscal_rows.risks: An open amount charged to the chambers' existing appropriations may crowd out their other activities or delay the Commission's start.

fiscal_rows.existing: Included in the annual General Appropriations Act, including any deficiency in the current year.
fiscal_rows.consideration: About P96.1 million to P179.8 million a year for PS and MOOE over the remaining two years of the three-year term.
fiscal_rows.recommendation: The requirements may be included in the budgets of the Senate and the House of Representatives in the succeeding GAA (FY 2028 at the earliest), subject to fiscal space; funding should end with the Commission's three-year term.
fiscal_rows.risks: Without a clear end date in the appropriations, funding may continue beyond the Commission's mandate.

fiscal_rows.existing: A full-time Executive Director with the rank of Executive Director IV (Salary Grade 29).
fiscal_rows.consideration: About P3.0 million a year with mandatory benefits (SG 29, Step 1, 2026 salary schedule).
fiscal_rows.recommendation: The position title and salary grade are subject to evaluation under the Compensation and Position Classification System, consistent with comparable positions in congressional commissions.
fiscal_rows.risks: A grade above comparable positions may create pay distortions.

fiscal_rows.existing: A Technical Secretariat headed by the Executive Director, who hires temporary, contractual or consultancy personnel and determines their compensation.
fiscal_rows.consideration: The estimate assumes 76 to 124 positions; the actual staffing should be smaller if personnel are detailed from the two chambers.
fiscal_rows.recommendation: The organizational structure and staffing pattern should be submitted for review, and the compensation of contractual and consultancy personnel should follow existing rules; the Secretariat should be co-terminous with the Commission.
fiscal_rows.risks: Open authority to set compensation may raise personnel cost above standard rates.

fiscal_rows.provision: Section 8 (Philippine Institute for Development Studies as Research Arm)
fiscal_rows.existing: PIDS, an existing agency, serves as research arm.
fiscal_rows.consideration: Requirements to be charged to the existing agency's budget.
fiscal_rows.recommendation: Any added requirement of PIDS should be included in its own budget proposal, or covered by the Commission's appropriations through a memorandum of agreement.
fiscal_rows.risks: Competes with PIDS's other research commitments.

fiscal_rows.provision: Section 5 (Composition of AGRICOM); Section 9 (Agriculture and Fisheries Legislation and Policy Advisory Council)
fiscal_rows.existing: Twelve legislators serving without compensation, with allowable expenses; an advisory council of experts.
fiscal_rows.consideration: Travel, meeting and honoraria expenses form part of MOOE in the estimate.
fiscal_rows.recommendation: Allowable expenses and honoraria should be limited to actual travel and meetings, consistent with existing rules (EO No. 77, s. 2019).

duplications.existing: Congressional Oversight Committee on Agricultural and Fisheries Modernization, RA No. 8435 (Sections 114 to 116)
duplications.note: Both bodies review the agriculture and fisheries sector and report or recommend actions to Congress.
duplications.assessment: The bill adds a body without changing or abolishing the existing committee; the functions should be delineated in line with the principles of RA No. 12231.

recommendation.label: Interpose no objection, subject to amendments
issues: Define the scope of the national assessment (Part IV)
Add ex officio, non-voting department secretaries (Part IV)
Delineate the Commission's functions from those of the RA No. 8435 oversight committee (Parts IV and VI)
Provide for periodic and final reports (Part IV)
State the initial amount and limit funding to the three-year term (Part V)

referrals.why: Salary grade of the Executive Director, and the structure, staffing and compensation of the Technical Secretariat
Appropriations language: initial charge to the appropriations of the two chambers and inclusion in the succeeding GAA
Budgetary requirements to be charged to the budgets of the Senate and the House of Representatives (Congress), and any added requirement of PIDS (research arm, Section 8), both under its coverage
Possible duplication with the RA No. 8435 oversight committee, in light of RA No. 12231

V: 5.1 Based on the organization and staffing standards and existing rules on maintenance and capital outlays, the creation of the Commission would require about P107.1 million to P196.8 million in its first year, consisting of Personnel Services of P66.7 million to P132.9 million, Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses of P29.5 million to P46.8 million, and Capital Outlay of P11.0 million to P17.0 million, which is a one-time requirement. Thereafter, about P96.1 million to P179.8 million would be needed every year for the remainder of its three-year term. The estimate assumes a Secretariat of 76 to 124 positions and should be lower if personnel are detailed from the two chambers.

5.2 As regards the initial funding under Section 13 of HB No. 2322, the requirement may be charged to the available appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives, as provided. However, the amount should be stated, as discussed in Part IV, so that it can be programmed within the two chambers' budgets.

5.3 The succeeding requirements may be included in the budgets of the Senate and the House of Representatives in the succeeding GAA, subject to fiscal space, and should end with the Commission's term.

5.4 As regards the Executive Director (Section 6) and the Technical Secretariat (Section 7), the position title, salary grade and staffing pattern are subject to evaluation under the Compensation and Position Classification System, and the compensation of contractual and consultancy personnel should follow existing rules. Allowable expenses of the members and the advisory council (Sections 5 and 9) should be limited to actual travel and meetings, consistent with EO No. 77, s. 2019.
VI: 6.1 Section 11 of HB No. 2322 appears to overlap with the functions of the Congressional Oversight Committee on Agricultural and Fisheries Modernization under Sections 114 to 116 of RA No. 8435, which likewise reviews the sector and reports to Congress. The bill does not provide for the abolition, merger or transfer of the existing committee or its functions. While the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231), signed on August 4, 2025, covers the Executive branch, its Section 21 requires the other branches to observe its principles of avoiding unnecessarily overlapping or duplicating functions. In this regard, the bill may be revisited to delineate the functions of the two bodies or to provide for the Commission to build on the work of the existing committee.
VII: 7.1 This Department interposes no objection to the proposed measure, subject to the incorporation of the recommendations.

7.2 In particular, the following should be considered: (a) defining the scope of the national assessment; (b) the participation of the concerned department secretaries as ex officio, non-voting members; (c) delineating the Commission's functions from those of the oversight committee under RA No. 8435; (d) the submission of periodic and final reports; and (e) stating the initial amount of funding and limiting it to the Commission's three-year term.
